What to Bring

What to Expect

60 minutes. Live Hoops.

Every tryout follows the same structure so every player is evaluated the same way.

Check-in

15 min early

Arrive in your athletic clothes. Pick up your numbered jersey, sign the medical waiver, and warm up with the team. Coaches introduce themselves and walk through the agenda.

Skill Stations

Next 15 min

Ball handling & footwork warmup — Coaches are on the move so every player is seen by every evaluator.

Live 5-on-5

Next 40 min

Random teams, full-court games. This is where coaches see decision-making, spacing, communication, and competitive instinct in real time.

Wrap & Q&A

Final 5 min

Group huddle. Coach takes quick questions and thanks everyone for coming out. Reminds kids of future tryouts & when teams will be decided by.

Full Transparency

How players are evaluated.

No politics. No favorites. Every coach grades every player on the same four pillars, with the same rubric.
Here's exactly what we look for, in the order we weigh it.

30%Weight

Effort

Are they playing hard, every rep? Effort is the only thing every player can control, and it tells us everything about how they'll respond to a tough season.

  • Sprints back on defense without being told
  • Boxes out on every rebound, every possession
  • Dives for loose balls. Communicates loudly.
  • First in line for every drill
20%Weight

Skill

Can they execute the fundamentals at game speed? We're not looking for finished products at age 10, we're looking for a foundation we can build on.

  • Clean ball-handling with both hands under pressure
  • Repeatable shooting form (not necessarily a hot streak)
  • Active defensive stance and lateral quickness
  • Finishing with control around the rim
30%Weight

Coachability

When a coach gives feedback, what happens next? This is the single biggest predictor of whether a player makes the leap from middle school to varsity.

  • Eye contact when receiving instruction
  • Adjusts on the very next rep
  • Body language stays positive after a missed shot or turnover
  • Picks up teammates verbally and physically
20%Weight

Game Understanding

Do they see the floor before the play happens? Court IQ separates good athletes from real basketball players. It's the hardest thing to teach.

  • Knows when to pass vs. when to attack
  • Reads help defense and finds the open teammate
  • Spaces the floor without being reminded
  • Recognizes mismatches and exploits them
Player Landing SPots.

Regardless of if you make the A team or the B team, placement is about putting your player in the right environment to grow.

Multiple Coaches Score Each Player.

No single coach decides where a kid goes. Scores are averaged and reviewed by the program director & coaches before placements go out.

    Parent FAQ

    The questions we always get.

    Real answers. If yours isn't here, email mundeleinboysbasketball@gmail.com — we respond within 24 hours.

    What if my child can't make their assigned tryout day?

    We will post an official make-up day from 9 AM to 12 PM. Email the coach as soon as you know about a conflict — we'll fit you in.

    What's the time commitment if my player makes a team?

    Two practices per week (60-90 min each, evenings), 2 weekend tournaments between November and February, and 14 regular season games. We share the full calendar at first practice.

    How are A and B teams decided?

    Our coaches independently score every player on the four criteria above. Scores are averaged, reviewed by the program director, and balanced for grade-level chemistry. Body language and attitude during evaluation matter — we're picking on more than just talent.

    What if my child has never played organized basketball?

    Show up. About a third of our 5th and 6th grade players have little to no prior experience. Coachability and effort outweigh experience every single time.

    Is financial aid available?

    Yes — fully and confidentially. Email mundeleinboysbasketball@gmail.com with the subject "Aid request." We will never turn a Mundelein kid away over money.

    When are season fees due?

    Season fee is $700 for all grades. It is invoiced after team placements go out on Nov 13 and is due Nov 16. Players also need a one-time uniform: a reversible jersey, shorts, and a white practice t-shirt that families keep. We sell jerseys to our families at cost, because we don't want to take any extra money from our families. Families who don't need a new size next season won't pay for jerseys again.

    What's the refund policy?

    Tryouts are free. After acceptance, season fees are refundable for 7 days after tryouts conclude.

    Can siblings try out together?

    Absolutely. Siblings will be evaluated in their own grade-and-gender group. Tryout slots are often scheduled back-to-back so most families only need one trip.

    Do I need to bring anything besides what's listed?

    If you have a printed copy of the medical waiver signed at home, it speeds up check-in. Otherwise, you can sign it at the door. That's it. We provide loaner basketballs if needed.
